newsitem.title: GERMANY: Colonia upbeat on UAP /Axa merger.
newsitem.headline: Colonia upbeat on UAP /Axa merger.

text.p: Colonia AG, the German unit of Union Assurances de Paris (UAP), on Tuesday said it welcomed its French parent's unexpected revelation of plans to merge with Axa.
UAP and Axa revealed their plans to merge earlier on Tuesday and analysts said Colonia would be a key aspect of the deal, giving Axa access to the German market.
"This will make us part of a real global player," Colonia spokesman Ulrich Bockrath told Reuters.

Colonia's shares raced ahead after the news in an overall firmer market, gaining over 13 percent to end IBIS dealings up 15.20 marks ($10.17) at 132 marks, having earlier touched a year high of 133 marks.
Bockrath said the alliance would mean the French group could overtake Germany's Allianz AG Holding in Europe.
Allianz took a relaxed line on the merger plans. "We congratulate them on the wedding," an Allianz spokesman told Reuters, declining further comment.
The move would not mean many changes for Colonia in Germany, where Axa currently has only one small direct insurance unit, Bockrath said.
UAP took control of Colonia three years ago and currently owns around 68 percent of the German group.
